correctness.rationale: Base Fourier transform gives lambda(theta)=2 sum_r(1-cos theta_r) in [0,4d], while path eigenvalues mu_j=2-2cos(pi j/m) are distinct and eigenvector amplitudes v_j(a)=sqrt(2/m)cos(pi j(a+.5)/m) (j>0). Visibility vanishes exactly when j(2a+1)=m(odd), giving (g-1)/2 invisible modes; the weighted temporal Vandermonde hence has rank min(p,m-(g-1)/2). A compact base-frequency range and uniformly bounded invertible row rescalings give stable frames exactly at full rank. At endpoint, Vandermonde determinant times exp(-tau lambda C_m) is smallest at lambda=4d. Its log derivative equals sum_{i<j} Delta/(exp(tau Delta)-1)-[4d C_m+sum_{i<j}mu_i], and log second derivative strictly negative; zero and infinity limits yield one maximum. The triangular Euler-Maclaurin formula has first correction -m/(2tau), and sum_{i<j}mu_i=m²(1-4/pi²)-2m+O(1); uniform smoothness, monotone implicit function give tau=s_d+c_d/m+O(m^-2). Independently integrated defining double integral with scipy and solved finite stationarity: d1 s=0.1682323819219894,c=0.0587318012130304, width-error times m at m=20,50,100 is .0597264,.0591269,.0589289, approaching c; d2 s=.1003350654556886,c=.020539050871182. Finite computations corroborate but do not prove uniform asymptotic. Critical distinction: graph Laplacian is combinatorial, determinant not minimum frame eigenvalue.

final_claim: For the combinatorial Laplacian on G=Z^d square P_m, fixed transverse sensor site a at every base cell, p consecutive samples at times k tau have Fourier-fiber rank min(p,m-(g-1)/2) with g=gcd(2a+1,m); stable recovery of arbitrary l2 states occurs iff g=1,p>=m. With an endpoint a=0 and p=m, the square-root worst-fiber Gram determinant is W_m exp(-4d*m*(m-1)*tau/2) times a temporal Vandermonde product, with unique positive D-optimal tau including finite m=2 optimum; as width m increases it has a uniquely defined integral limit s_d and positive first-order c_d/m correction.
